theme: Nowcasting methods and packages: MIDAS, dynamic factor models, bridge equations, nowcasting with Google Trends, KPI nowcasting for companies

candidates.name: nowcasting-mexico
candidates.what_it_holds: Reproducible Snakemake pipeline nowcasting Mexican IGAE (economic-activity index) 2018-2024 using Banxico API series (exchange rate, CETES, M1, credit), INEGI flat files (industrial production, retail sales, unemployment), Google Trends (7 keywords) and Google Mobility (2020-2022). Implements AR(4), MIDAS, DFM, LASSO, Ridge, Random Forest with pseudo-out-of-sample evaluation, R+Python, Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20563443 for the writeup. No committed data files, but automated pull scripts for all sources.
candidates.why_useful: Direct template for gap #7 (LatAm regional travel/consumer volume, esp. Mexico DATATUR/INEGI-adjacent) and gap #17 (mixed-frequency nowcasting methods incl. MIDAS/DFM combined with Google Trends and mobility data) — could be adapted to nowcast ABNB LatAm nights using Mexico macro + Trends + mobility as regressors, and the MIDAS/DFM code is directly reusable methodology.
candidates.size_hint: pipeline repo, no large committed data; pulls INEGI/Banxico/Trends/Mobility on run

candidates.name: Nowcasting
candidates.what_it_holds: New York Fed's own dynamic-factor-model nowcasting codebase (MATLAB/R/Python variants across forks) underlying the NY Fed Staff Nowcast — implements the Giannone-Reichlin-Small DFM/Kalman-filter mixed-frequency framework used to nowcast US GDP from a large panel of mixed-frequency macro releases.
candidates.why_useful: Canonical, most-cited open implementation of the DFM nowcasting method (gap #17); useful as the estimation engine to build an ABNB-KPI-specific mixed-frequency nowcast (nights/ADR vs macro + alt-data releases) rather than reinventing the Kalman filter/EM code.

candidates.name: nowcast_lstm
candidates.what_it_holds: LSTM-based mixed-frequency nowcasting library for economic data (Python, also ported to R/MATLAB/Julia); handles unbalanced/ragged-edge mixed-frequency panels the way MIDAS/DFM do but with a neural net; from the same author group as the World Bank/UN nowcasting benchmark paper.
candidates.why_useful: Alternative/competitor method to MIDAS and DFM for the KPI-nowcasting problem in gap #17; benchmarked as best single method in dhopp1/nowcasting_benchmark below — a candidate engine for nowcasting ABNB nights/ADR from ragged alt-data releases (Trends, TSA, calendar-derived indices) ahead of quarter close.

candidates.name: nowcasting_benchmark
candidates.what_it_holds: Companion code (R + Python notebooks) to a published benchmarking article estimating 17 nowcasting/ML methods (ARMA, Bayesian MF-VAR, DFM, MIDAS, midasml, LSTM, XGBoost, elastic net, etc.) for quarterly US GDP using FRED data Q1 2002-Q3 2022, following Bok et al. (2018) NY Fed variable specification. No raw data committed (pulls FRED), but runnable example notebooks with FRED series list.
candidates.why_useful: A ready reference implementation and honest performance comparison across every mixed-frequency method named in gap #17 (MIDAS, DFM, bridge-style MF-VAR, midasml) — useful to pick and validate the estimation approach for an ABNB KPI nowcast before committing engineering time to one method.

candidates.name: Nowcasting_toolbox
candidates.what_it_holds: Code and templates accompanying Linzenich & Meunier (2024), 'Nowcasting Made Easier: a Toolbox for Real-Time Predictions,' ECB Working Paper No. 3004 — a general-purpose real-time nowcasting toolbox (bridge-equation and DFM style) built by ECB staff, designed to be adapted to any target series with mixed-frequency indicators.
candidates.why_useful: Directly on-theme for gap #17 (bridge equations, DFM); an ECB-authored, paper-backed toolbox is a credible, documented starting point for building the ABNB revenue/nights bridge-equation nowcast the team already uses conceptually (H1-to-H2 bridge, Q4 guide arithmetic).

candidates.name: nowcasting (R package)
candidates.what_it_holds: R package implementing Dynamic Factor Models with mixed frequencies and unbalanced panels (ragged-edge data), originally built for Brazilian central-bank-style nowcasting of GDP/activity indices.
candidates.why_useful: Reusable DFM engine for mixed-frequency/unbalanced-panel problems (gap #17); the ragged-edge handling is exactly the shape of the ABNB problem (macro releases and alt-data land at different times ahead of the print).

candidates.name: Deep_XF
candidates.what_it_holds: Python package for building explainable forecasting/nowcasting models combining deep neural nets with Dynamic Factor Models on time-series panels, single-line-of-code API; also includes signal-similarity matching and denoising utilities.
candidates.why_useful: Another off-the-shelf DFM+deep-learning nowcasting library (gap #17) that could shortcut building a KPI nowcast pipeline for ABNB nights/ADR from a mixed panel of alt-data signals.

candidates.name: Nowcasting-Python
candidates.what_it_holds: Python port/implementation of a nowcasting model (dynamic-factor/mixed-frequency style, per description "Python Nowcasting"); 135 stars but description is terse — needs closer inspection before relying on it.
candidates.why_useful: Potential lightweight Python DFM nowcasting implementation (gap #17) if it turns out to be a faithful port of the classic Giannone-Reichlin-Small model; flagged for follow-up rather than confirmed.

candidates.name: macro-nowcast-dfm
candidates.what_it_holds: "Production-ready" GDP nowcasting engine combining Mixed-Frequency Dynamic Factor Models (labelled MIDAS in the description, effectively DFM+MIDAS hybrid) and Kalman filtering to extract real-time macro health signals; small repo (3 stars).
candidates.why_useful: Small but on-theme MIDAS/DFM/Kalman-filter engine (gap #17) that could be inspected for a compact, dependency-light implementation to adapt for an ABNB consumer-strength nowcast.

candidates.name: GDP_Forecasting_With_MIDAS_Regressions
candidates.what_it_holds: Student/academic project forecasting GDP with MIDAS regressions using mixed-frequency macro indicators; includes data-prep, estimation, and evaluation code (2 stars).
candidates.why_useful: Small, readable MIDAS-in-Python worked example (gap #17); useful mainly as a teaching reference for implementing MIDAS weighting schemes (Almon lag etc.) rather than as a reusable package.

candidates.name: midas_capstone
candidates.what_it_holds: IE University capstone (2026) comparing MIDAS vs ARIMAX for forecasting US Consumer Energy CPI using weekly WTI oil futures data as the high-frequency indicator; includes CLM-SS (a novel MIDAS variant), LASSO-MIDAS, Kernel U-MIDAS, XGBoost and LSTM benchmarks.
candidates.why_useful: A recent (2026), reasonably rigorous academic comparison of several MIDAS variants against ML benchmarks on a real macro series (gap #17); the CLM-SS/LASSO-MIDAS/Kernel U-MIDAS code could be repurposed to mix weekly consumer/FX indicators into a quarterly ABNB KPI nowcast.

candidates.name: MIDAS-Nowcast
candidates.what_it_holds: Near-real-time forecasting of UK household savings using MIDAS regressions on mixed-frequency UK data (savings ratio target, higher-frequency indicators).
candidates.why_useful: On-theme MIDAS implementation (gap #17); UK household savings is a consumer-strength proxy loosely analogous to the OECD/consumer-confidence work already held, though geography (UK) is outside the team's core NA/APAC/LatAm focus.

candidates.name: tsecon
candidates.what_it_holds: High-performance time-series econometrics library, Rust core with a Python-first API; markets itself as "validated estimators, a 15-chapter guide, and honest inference by default" — general econometric toolkit (not nowcasting-specific per se, but came up under the nowcasting search and covers mixed-frequency-adjacent estimators).
candidates.why_useful: General-purpose, fast time-series econometrics engine that could underlie custom bridge-equation/MIDAS estimation for ABNB KPIs if existing pure-Python tools (statsmodels) are too slow for repeated point-in-time refits across W1/W2 windows.

candidates.name: microprediction
candidates.what_it_holds: "If you can measure it, consider it predicted" — an open, crowd-sourced real-time prediction/nowcasting platform and Python client where any published time series (economic, web-traffic, etc.) can be nowcast by a community of algorithms; includes APIs to pull live crowd-nowcasts of arbitrary streams.
candidates.why_useful: Not a data source itself, but a live nowcasting-as-a-service platform (gap #17, tangential to #4 point-in-time forecasts) — could in principle host or query a crowd-nowcast of a published economic series relevant to consumer/travel demand; more a curiosity than a direct fit, low priority.

notes: The theme is heavily crowded on GitHub by meteorological 'precipitation nowcasting' repos (deep-learning radar models) which are irrelevant noise from the bare 'nowcasting' keyword search — filtered out. Plain-phrase gh search repos queries with multiple words ("midas regression python", "dynamic factor model nowcasting", "gtab google trends", "bridge equation forecasting") consistently returned zero results even though matching repos exist (found via topic filters and single-word queries instead) — gh search repos seems to require narrower/topic-based queries or exact substring matches rather than free-text; worth flagging to other scouts using this modality. No repo found that mirrors gtab (anchored/comparable Google Trends) specifically as a maintained package beyond the original gtab project itself (not re-verified here, likely already known). No KPI-nowcasting-for-a-specific-company repo (e.g., nowcasting a public company's revenue print from alt data) turned up; everything on-theme was macro/GDP-level nowcasting methodology, which is still directly reusable for gap #17's stated ask (MIDAS, DFM, bridge equations). Recommend a follow-up scout specifically on 'gtab' anchored-trends packages and on earnings-surprise/alt-data nowcasting for single companies (not macro), since this pass's keyword set skewed macro-econometrics.
